title: Numerals in every case, years and statistics
objectives: I can say and read large numbers, from the hundreds to the billions, and use 'ти́сяча', 'мільйо́н' and 'мілья́рд' with the genitive plural.
I can put cardinal numerals and the nouns they count into every case, as in 'з двома́ дру́зями' and 'у п’яти́ міста́х'.
I can say years, decades and centuries, and say in which year something happened or someone was born.
I can count people and plural-only things with 'дво́є' and 'тро́є', and say 'both' with 'о́бидва' and 'о́бидві'.
I can give and understand simple statistics with 'полови́на', 'чверть', 'півтора́' and percentages.

vocabulary.note: A noun in form: 'дві ти́сячі', 'п’ять ти́сяч', instrumental 'ти́сячею'. What it counts follows in the genitive plural. On its own it means one thousand, with no 'одна́'.

example.source: This phone costs a thousand hryvnias.

vocabulary.note: Genitive 'мільйо́на'; 'два мільйо́ни', 'п’ять мільйо́нів'. What it counts follows in the genitive plural.

example.target: У цьо́му мі́сті живе́ мільйо́н люде́й.
example.source: A million people live in this city.
example.source_literal: In this city lives million of-people.

vocabulary.note: A thousand million, as in American English. Genitive 'мілья́рда'; 'два мілья́рди', 'п’ять мілья́рдів'.

example.target: На Землі́ живе́ бі́льше ніж ві́сім мілья́рдів люде́й.
example.source: More than eight billion people live on Earth.
example.source_literal: On Earth lives more than eight of-billions of-people.

vocabulary.note: What it divides follows in the genitive. As a subject it takes a singular verb, feminine in the past.
Genitive 'чве́рті'; 'три чве́рті', three quarters. What it divides follows in the genitive.

example.target: Чверть студе́нтів ї́здить до університе́ту на метро́.
example.source: A quarter of the students take the metro to the university.
example.source_literal: Quarter of-students goes to university on metro.

vocabulary.note: With masculine and neuter nouns; 'півтори́' with feminine nouns. The noun follows in the genitive singular: 'півтора́ ро́ку', 'півтори́ годи́ни'.

example.source: I need a kilo and a half of potatoes.

vocabulary.note: Genitive 'відсо́тка'; 'два відсо́тки', 'п’ять відсо́тків'. The sign '%' is read as this word.

example.target: Сього́дні все на два́дцять відсо́тків деше́вше.
example.source: Today everything is twenty percent cheaper.
example.source_literal: Today everything by twenty of-percents cheaper.

vocabulary.source: two, of people or plural-only things
vocabulary.note: For men, mixed groups, children and plural-only nouns, never for feminine nouns. The noun follows in the genitive plural. Other cases take the forms of 'два': 'двох', 'двом', 'двома́'.

vocabulary.source: three, of people or plural-only things
vocabulary.note: Used like 'дво́є'. Other cases take the forms of 'три': 'трьох', 'трьом', 'трьома́'.

example.target: Нас тро́є: Окса́на, Тара́с і я.
example.source: There are three of us: Oksana, Taras and me.
example.source_literal: Of-us three: Oksana, Taras and I.

vocabulary.note: With masculine and neuter nouns; 'о́бидві' with feminine nouns. The noun follows in the nominative plural, as after 'два'. Other cases: 'обо́х', 'обо́м', 'обома́'.

example.source: I know both of these cities.

vocabulary.note: From 'сто' and 'лі́то', summer, which once also meant a year: 'a hundred summers'. Locative 'у столі́тті', genitive plural 'столі́ть'.

example.target: Ця ха́та стої́ть тут уже́ столі́ття.
example.source: This house has stood here for a century.
example.source_literal: This house stands here already century.

vocabulary.note: A period of ten years, built like 'столі́ття' from 'де́сять'. A named decade, such as the nineties, is said with 'ро́ки'.

example.target: Я не був у Льво́ві ці́ле десятилі́ття.
example.source: I haven't been to Lviv for a whole decade.
example.source_literal: I not was in Lviv whole decade.

vocabulary.note: Used in the singular. The place follows in the genitive: 'насе́лення мі́ста'.

example.source: The city's population is very young.
Sam has been to five countries.

example.target: О́ля вже до́бре раху́є до ста.
example.source: Olia can already count to a hundred.
example.source_literal: Olia already well counts to hundred.

vocabulary.note: A written digit, and in speech a figure in statistics. Genitive plural 'цифр'. A number as a quantity is 'число́'.
Goes before a number, which keeps its own form.

example.source: It's about two kilometers to the station.

vocabulary.note: The word of statistics and formal text, mostly in the forms 'стано́вить' and 'стано́влять', with the amount in the accusative. It has no perfective partner in this meaning.

example.source: The ticket price is three hundred hryvnias.

vocabulary.note: Past 'народи́вся', 'народи́лася', 'народи́лися'. Imperfective 'народжува́тися'. The '-ся' does not mean 'self' here.

example.source: My dad was born in Odesa.

dialogues.title: Figures in the news
dialogues.context: Taras and Sam are having coffee at Andrii's café, and Taras reads Sam the results of a city survey in the news on his phone: how the people of Kyiv get to work. The friends say 'ти' to each other. 'На маши́ні' means by car, and 'Торо́нто' is Toronto, a large city in Canada.

lines.speaker: Тара́с
lines.target: Се́ме, послу́хай, що тут пи́шуть. У Ки́єві живу́ть прибли́зно три мільйо́ни люде́й.
lines.source: Sam, listen to what it says here. About three million people live in Kyiv.
lines.source_literal: Sam, listen, what here they-write. In Kyiv live approximately three millions of-people.

lines.speaker: Сем
lines.target: Три мільйо́ни? Як у Торо́нто. А я ду́мав, що Ки́їв бі́льший.
lines.source: Three million? The same as Toronto. I thought Kyiv was bigger.
lines.source_literal: Three millions? As in Toronto. And I thought that Kyiv bigger.

lines.speaker: Тара́с
lines.target: А ось і́нші ци́фри. Со́рок відсо́тків люде́й ї́здять на робо́ту на метро́.
lines.source: And here are some other figures. Forty percent of people take the metro to work.
lines.source_literal: And here other figures. Forty of-percents of-people go to work on metro.

lines.speaker: Сем
lines.target: Со́рок? Я ду́мав, що полови́на. Вра́нці в метро́ ду́же бага́то люде́й.
lines.source: Forty? I thought it was half. In the morning the metro is full of people.
lines.source_literal: Forty? I thought that half. In-the-morning in metro very many of-people.

lines.speaker: Тара́с
lines.target: Ні, тут пи́шуть «со́рок». Чверть ї́здить авто́бусом, а п’ятна́дцять відсо́тків хо́дять на робо́ту, бо живу́ть бли́зько.
lines.source: No, it says 'forty' here. A quarter go by bus, and fifteen percent walk to work, because they live close by.
lines.source_literal: No, here they-write «forty». Quarter goes by-bus, and fifteen of-percents go to work, because they-live near.

lines.speaker: Сем
lines.target: Я раху́ю: со́рок, два́дцять п’ять і п’ятна́дцять. Це вісімдеся́т. А де ще два́дцять?
lines.source: Let me count: forty, twenty-five and fifteen. That's eighty. Where are the other twenty?
lines.source_literal: I count: forty, twenty five and fifteen. This eighty. And where still twenty?

lines.speaker: Тара́с
lines.target: Ці лю́ди ї́здять на маши́ні. Тут усе́ є.
lines.source: Those people go by car. It's all here.
lines.source_literal: These people go on car. Here everything is.

lines.speaker: Сем
lines.target: А скі́льки люде́й вони́ запита́ли?
lines.source: And how many people did they ask?
lines.source_literal: And how-many of-people they asked?

lines.speaker: Тара́с
lines.target: Ти́сячу.
lines.source: A thousand.
lines.source_literal: Thousand.

lines.speaker: Сем
lines.target: Ти́сячу з трьох мільйо́нів? Це ду́же ма́ло!
lines.source: A thousand out of three million? That's very few!
lines.source_literal: Thousand from three millions? This very few!

lines.speaker: Тара́с
lines.target: Ні, для таки́х цифр ти́сячі до́сить.
lines.source: No, a thousand is enough for figures like these.
lines.source_literal: No, for such figures of-thousand enough.

lines.speaker: Сем
lines.target: Мо́жливо. Але́ за́втра вра́нці я сам пораху́ю люде́й у метро́.
lines.source: Maybe. But tomorrow morning I'll count the people in the metro myself.
lines.source_literal: Possibly. But tomorrow in-the-morning I myself will-count people in metro.

lines.speaker: Тара́с
lines.target: Усі́ три мільйо́ни? Ти бу́деш рахува́ти ці́лий рік!
lines.source: All three million? You'll be counting for a whole year!
lines.source_literal: All three millions? You will to-count whole year!

dialogues.title: A family in years
dialogues.context: Oksana has drawn her family tree, with everyone's year of birth, as a birthday present for her grandmother. Sam looks at it at her home. They are friends and say 'ти'. 'Ону́ки' are grandchildren; one grandson is 'ону́к'.

lines.speaker: Сем
lines.target: Окса́но, що це? Тут так бага́то цифр!
lines.source: Oksana, what's this? There are so many figures here!
lines.source_literal: Oksana, what this? Here so many of-figures!

lines.speaker: Окса́на
lines.target: Це на́ша сім’я́ й ро́ки наро́дження. Я роблю́ це для бабу́сі, на її́ день наро́дження.
lines.source: It's our family and everyone's year of birth. I'm making it for Grandma, for her birthday.
lines.source_literal: This our family and years of-birth. I make this for grandma, on her day of-birth.

lines.speaker: Сем
lines.target: А хто тут найста́рший?
lines.source: And who's the oldest here?

lines.speaker: Окса́на
lines.target: Діду́сь. Він народи́вся в ти́сяча дев’ятсо́т со́рок п’я́тому ро́ці.
lines.source: Grandpa. He was born in 1945.
lines.source_literal: Grandpa. He was-born in thousand nine-hundred forty fifth year.

lines.speaker: Сем
lines.target: А бабу́ся?
lines.source: And Grandma?

lines.speaker: Окса́на
lines.target: Вона́ на три ро́ки моло́дша. Вона́ народи́лася в ти́сяча дев’ятсо́т со́рок восьмо́му.
lines.source: She's three years younger. She was born in 1948.
lines.source_literal: She by three years younger. She was-born in thousand nine-hundred forty eighth.

lines.speaker: Сем
lines.target: А скі́льки в них діте́й?
lines.source: And how many children do they have?
lines.source_literal: And how-many at them of-children?

lines.speaker: Окса́на
lines.target: Дво́є, дві до́ньки: моя́ ма́ма й ті́тка. О́бидві народи́лися в сімдеся́тих ро́ках, як і мій та́то.
lines.source: Two, two daughters: my mom and my aunt. Both were born in the seventies, like my dad.
lines.source_literal: Two, two daughters: my mom and aunt. Both were-born in seventieth years, as also my dad.

lines.speaker: Сем
lines.target: А ти й твій брат?
lines.source: And you and your brother?

lines.speaker: Окса́на
lines.target: Брат народи́вся в ти́сяча дев’ятсо́т дев’яно́сто шо́стому, а я в дві ти́сячі четве́ртому. Між на́ми ві́сім ро́ків.
lines.source: My brother was born in 1996, and I was born in 2004. There are eight years between us.
lines.source_literal: Brother was-born in thousand nine-hundred ninety sixth, and I in two thousands fourth. Between us eight of-years.

lines.speaker: Сем
lines.target: А це хто? Тут ще одне́ ім’я́.
lines.source: And who's this? There's one more name here.
lines.source_literal: And this who? Here still one name.

lines.speaker: Окса́на
lines.target: Це О́ля, до́нька мого́ бра́та. Вона́ народи́лася в дві ти́сячі два́дцять пе́ршому ро́ці.
lines.source: That's Olia, my brother's daughter. She was born in 2021.
lines.source_literal: This Olia, daughter of-my of-brother. She was-born in two thousands twenty first year.

lines.speaker: Сем
lines.target: У ті́тки теж є ді́ти?
lines.source: Does your aunt have children too?
lines.source_literal: At aunt also are children?

lines.speaker: Окса́на
lines.target: Так, дво́є, син і до́нька. Тому́ в бабу́сі й діду́ся че́тверо ону́ків.
lines.source: Yes, two, a son and a daughter. So Grandma and Grandpa have four grandchildren.
lines.source_literal: Yes, two, son and daughter. So at grandma and grandpa four of-grandchildren.

grammar.title: Numerals in every case: оди́н, два, три, чоти́ри
grammar.explanation:
So far you have used numbers mainly in the nominative, and as the object of a verb when they count things. In those two places the number decides the form of the noun: 'два ро́ки', 'п’ять ро́ків'. But a cardinal numeral changes for case, like a noun or an adjective, and the rule for the noun after it holds only in the nominative and in the accusative of things.

In every other case the numeral and the noun simply stand in the same case, and the noun is plural, as it is in English after 'two':

- genitive: 'до трьох міст', up to three cities
- dative: 'трьом міста́м', to three cities
- instrumental: 'з трьома́ міста́ми', with three cities
- locative: 'у трьох міста́х', in three cities

So the special forms disappear. After 'з', with, you say 'з двома́ дру́зями', with the same instrumental plural 'дру́зями' that you would use without the number. 'Дві' exists only in the nominative and the accusative; in the other cases one form serves all three genders: 'двох браті́в', 'двох сесте́р'. The instrumental forms 'двома́', 'трьома́' and 'чотирма́' are stressed on the last syllable, and 'чотирма́' has no soft sign.

The accusative depends on what is counted, by the rule you know from the plural. With things it is the same as the nominative: 'Я купи́в два квитки́.' With people and animals it is the same as the genitive, for the numeral and for the noun: 'Я зна́ю двох програмі́стів.'

'Оди́н' changes like an adjective and agrees with its noun in every case. The forms below are the genitive, the dative, the instrumental and the locative; the feminine adds its accusative 'одну́', and the masculine accusative is 'одного́' with people:

- masculine and neuter: 'одного́', 'одному́', 'одни́м', 'на одно́му'
- feminine: 'одніє́ї', 'одні́й', 'одніє́ю', 'на одні́й'

The feminine forms 'одно́ї' and 'одно́ю' are also correct. A noun after 'оди́н' stays singular in every case: 'з одни́м дру́гом', with one friend.

examples.source: I live with two friends.
We were in three cities.
I help three students.
We're inviting three neighbors.
This table is for four people.

grammar.title: From п’ять up: case forms, the hundreds, ти́сяча and мільйо́н
grammar.explanation:
The numbers from 'п’ять' to 'два́дцять', and 'три́дцять', change for case with endings of their own: '-и' in the genitive, the dative and the locative, and '-ма' in the instrumental. Each also has a second set of forms built like 'чотирьо́х', with '-ьох', '-ьом' and '-ьома'. Both sets are standard, and the second is especially common with people:

- genitive: 'п’яти́' or 'п’ятьо́х'
- dative: 'п’яти́' or 'п’ятьо́м'
- instrumental: 'п’ятьма́' or 'п’ятьома́'
- locative: 'на п’яти́' or 'на п’ятьо́х'

In these forms of 'п’ять' to 'де́сять', 'два́дцять' and 'три́дцять' the stress is on the ending. 'П’ятдеся́т', 'шістдеся́т', 'сімдеся́т' and 'вісімдеся́т' change only their second part, in the same way: 'п’ятдесяти́' or 'п’ятдесятьо́х', 'п’ятдесятьма́' or 'п’ятдесятьома́'. In 'шість', 'сім' and 'ві́сім' the 'і' becomes 'е' or 'о' in the forms in '-и', by the rule of closed and open syllables: 'шести́', 'семи́', 'восьми́'. The other forms keep the 'і': 'шістьма́', 'вісьма́', 'вісьмо́х', and for 'сім' the forms 'сімо́х' and 'сімома́', with no soft sign because 'ь' never follows 'м'. The instrumental of 'сім' is 'сьома́' or 'сімома́'. Three numbers have one form for every case except the nominative and the accusative: 'со́рок' has 'сорока́', 'дев’яно́сто' has 'дев’яно́ста' and 'сто' has 'ста'.

The noun follows the same rule as with 'два'. In the nominative and in the accusative of things it is in the genitive plural ('п’ять міст'); in the other cases it takes the case of the numeral ('у п’яти́ міста́х', 'з п’ятьма́ студе́нтами'). For people in the accusative both forms are used: 'Я ба́чу п’ять студе́нтів.' and 'Я ба́чу п’ятьо́х студе́нтів.' In a compound number every word changes, in careful speech and in writing: 'до двадцяти́ п’яти́ ро́ків', up to twenty-five years.

The hundreds are built from a unit and a form of 'сто', and they repeat the rule of the noun after a number, frozen into one word:

- 'дві́сті' (200), with 'сті', an old form used for exactly two of something
- 'три́ста' (300) and 'чоти́риста' (400), with 'ста', an old plural, as in 'три ро́ки'
- 'п’ятсо́т' (500) to 'дев’ятсо́т' (900), with 'сот', the genitive plural, as in 'п’ять ро́ків'

In the other cases both parts change. The genitive is the form needed most: 'двохсо́т', 'трьохсо́т', 'п’ятисо́т', as in 'до п’ятисо́т гри́вень', up to five hundred hryvnias.

'Ти́сяча', 'мільйо́н' and 'мілья́рд' name numbers, and Ukrainian school grammar lists them with the numerals, but in form they are nouns: 'ти́сяча' is feminine, 'мільйо́н' and 'мілья́рд' are masculine, and each has a singular and a plural. A number before them follows the usual rule, and what they count always follows in the genitive plural:

- 'ти́сяча гри́вень', 'дві ти́сячі гри́вень', 'п’ять ти́сяч гри́вень'
- 'оди́н мільйо́н люде́й', 'три мільйо́ни люде́й', 'п’ять мільйо́нів люде́й'

In the other cases they change as nouns, and the counted noun stays in the genitive plural: 'з ти́сячею гри́вень', with a thousand hryvnias.

A large number is said from the largest part to the smallest, with no word for 'and': 'ти́сяча дві́сті' (1,200), 'три ти́сячі п’ятсо́т со́рок' (3,540), 'два мільйо́ни сімсо́т ти́сяч' (2,700,000).

examples.source: I need five hundred hryvnias.
We talked with five students.
The tickets cost up to two hundred hryvnias.

examples.target: Ця кни́га ко́штує ти́сячу дві́сті гри́вень.
examples.source: This book costs twelve hundred hryvnias.
examples.source_literal: This book costs thousand two-hundred of-hryvnias.

examples.target: До Льво́ва прибли́зно п’ятсо́т со́рок кіломе́трів.
examples.source: It's about five hundred forty kilometers to Lviv.
examples.source_literal: To Lviv approximately five-hundred forty of-kilometers.

grammar.title: Years, decades and centuries
grammar.explanation:
Ukrainian names a year with an ordinal numeral: 1991 is 'the one thousand nine hundred ninety-first year'. As in dates, only the last word is an ordinal. The words before it are cardinal numerals, and they never change, whatever the case of the phrase; only the ordinal and 'рік' change:

- 'ти́сяча дев’ятсо́т дев’яно́сто пе́рший рік', 1991
- 'у ти́сяча дев’ятсо́т дев’яно́сто пе́ршому ро́ці', in 1991

To say in which year something happens, use 'у' or 'в' with the locative, as for a month. The ordinal takes the adjective ending '-ому', and 'рік' becomes 'ро́ці', with 'і' changed to 'о' as in 'ро́ку', and 'к' changed to 'ц' before '-і', as in 'кни́га', 'у кни́зі'. The question is 'У яко́му ро́ці?' In a full date the year follows the month in the genitive, as 'of' the year: 'два́дцять четве́ртого се́рпня ти́сяча дев’ятсо́т дев’яно́сто пе́ршого ро́ку', on August 24, 1991. When the year is clear from the conversation, 'ро́ці' is often left out: 'Він народи́вся в ти́сяча дев’ятсо́т со́рок п’я́тому.'

Years from 2001 on begin with 'дві ти́сячі', which stays in the nominative: 'у дві ти́сячі пе́ршому ро́ці', 'у дві ти́сячі два́дцять п’я́тому ро́ці'. The year 2000 is one word, the ordinal 'двохти́сячний': 'у двохти́сячному ро́ці'.

The ordinals of the round numbers are built on the cardinals:

- 'сороко́вий', fortieth
- 'п’ятдеся́тий', 'шістдеся́тий', 'сімдеся́тий', 'вісімдеся́тий', fiftieth to eightieth
- 'дев’яно́стий', ninetieth
- 'со́тий', hundredth
- 'ти́сячний', thousandth

A decade such as the nineties is named by the plural of the ordinal with 'ро́ки': 'дев’яно́сті ро́ки', the nineties. 'In the nineties' is 'у дев’яно́стих ро́ках', with the locative plural, which for ordinals ends in '-их', as for adjectives. Where the century is not clear, add it in the genitive: 'у шістдеся́тих ро́ках двадця́того столі́ття', in the 1960s. The noun 'десятилі́ття' is a decade as a length of time, ten years: 'ці́ле десятилі́ття', a whole decade.

A century is 'столі́ття', a neuter noun, so its ordinal is neuter: 'двадця́те столі́ття', the twentieth century; 'у двадця́тому столі́тті', in the twentieth century; 'у два́дцять пе́ршому столі́тті', in the twenty-first century, where again only the last word is an ordinal.

grammar.title: Collective numerals: дво́є, тро́є; both: о́бидва, о́бидві
grammar.explanation:
Ukrainian has a second set of numerals for counting people and some things as a group: the collective numerals 'дво́є', 'тро́є', 'че́тверо', 'п’я́теро' and so on. 'Дво́є діте́й' means 'two children', and presents them as a pair, a group of two. After a collective numeral the noun is in the genitive plural, as after 'п’ять': 'дво́є діте́й', 'тро́є дру́зів'.

Collective numerals are used with:

- nouns for men, and for groups of men and women: 'дво́є браті́в', 'тро́є студе́нтів'
- 'ді́ти': 'дво́є діте́й'
- plural-only nouns, which 'два', 'три' and 'чоти́ри' cannot count: 'дво́є штані́в', two pairs of trousers
- the pronouns 'нас', 'вас' and 'їх', to say how many people there are: 'Нас дво́є.', There are two of us.

They are not used with feminine nouns: two sisters are 'дві сестри́'. With nouns for men both kinds are correct: 'два брати́' and 'дво́є браті́в'. In the other cases a collective numeral takes the forms of 'два', 'три' and 'чоти́ри': 'з двома́ дітьми́', with two children; 'Я ба́чу трьох діте́й.', I see three children.

In 'Нас дво́є.' the pronoun is in the genitive, literally 'of-us two', and the sentence has no verb in the present. In the past the verb is neuter singular: 'Нас було́ тро́є.', There were three of us.

'О́бидва', both, is used with masculine and neuter nouns, and 'о́бидві' with feminine nouns. Like 'два' and 'дві', they take the nominative plural: 'о́бидва брати́', 'о́бидві сестри́'. In the other cases they have one set of forms for every gender: 'обо́х', 'обо́м', 'обома́', 'на обо́х'. For a man and a woman together, and with plural-only nouns, Ukrainian uses the collective numeral 'о́боє': 'Мої́ батьки́ о́боє працю́ють у шко́лі.'

grammar.title: Proportions, percentages and statistics
grammar.explanation:
Ukrainian names most proportions with nouns. 'Полови́на', half, and 'чверть', quarter, are feminine nouns, and what they divide follows in the genitive, where English uses 'of': 'полови́на студе́нтів', half of the students; 'чверть насе́лення', a quarter of the population. They are counted like other nouns: 'три чве́рті', three quarters. As the subject of a sentence 'полови́на' and 'чверть' are singular, so the verb is singular too, and feminine in the past: 'Полови́на студе́нтів працю́є.', 'Полови́на студе́нтів працюва́ла.' After 'три чве́рті' the verb is usually plural, as after 'три': 'Три чве́рті студе́нтів гово́рять англі́йською.' The shorter word 'пів', which you know from telling the time ('пів на во́сьму'), also means half, and a noun after it is in the genitive: 'пів кілогра́ма', half a kilogram.

'Півтора́' means one and a half. It is built from 'пів' and an old word for 'second', so it means 'half of the second'. Use 'півтора́' with masculine and neuter nouns and 'півтори́' with feminine nouns, and put the noun in the genitive singular: 'півтора́ ро́ку', a year and a half; 'півтора́ мільйо́на', one and a half million; 'півтори́ годи́ни', an hour and a half; 'півтори́ ти́сячі', fifteen hundred.

'Відсо́ток', percent, is a masculine noun and is counted like any noun: 'оди́н відсо́ток', 'два відсо́тки', 'п’ять відсо́тків', 'два́дцять оди́н відсо́ток'. What it measures follows in the genitive: 'со́рок відсо́тків люде́й', forty percent of people. The sign '%' is read as this word, in the form the number needs. The question is 'Скі́льки відсо́тків?'

Statistics use a few more patterns:

- 'прибли́зно' before a number, which keeps its own form: 'прибли́зно три мільйо́ни люде́й'
- 'бі́льше ніж' and 'ме́нше ніж' with the nominative, as in comparisons: 'бі́льше ніж мільйо́н люде́й'
- 'стано́вити', to amount to, with the amount in the accusative: 'Ціна́ стано́вить ти́сячу гри́вень.'
- 'на' with the accusative for a difference: 'на два́дцять відсо́тків бі́льше', twenty percent more; 'на три ро́ки моло́дша', three years younger

When a number is the subject, the verb after 'два', 'три' and 'чоти́ри' is usually plural: 'Три студе́нти працю́ють.' After 'п’ять' and higher numbers, and after 'бі́льше ніж', it can be plural or singular, and both are correct. The singular presents the number as one amount, which is common in statistics, and in the past it is neuter: 'У мі́сті жило́ п’ять ти́сяч люде́й.'

grammar.title: Spelling and sound: мільйо́н, дев’ятсо́т, чотирьо́х and столі́ття
grammar.explanation:
Every new word and form in this unit can be read with the rules of the alphabet units and the unit on stress. The numerals bring up the points below.

The soft sign before 'о' and before 'йо' writes two different things. After a consonant, 'ьо' shows that the consonant is soft and that [ɔ] follows it directly, since the letter 'о' cannot show softness by itself: 'чотирьо́х' [t͡ʃɔtɪˈrʲɔx], 'трьох' [trʲɔx], 'п’ятьо́х' [pjɑˈtʲɔx]. In 'мільйо́н' [mʲilʲˈjɔn] a [j] is said between the soft 'л' and the vowel, and 'й' writes it, so the spelling is 'ьйо'. 'Мілья́рд' [mʲilʲˈjɑrd] has the same [lʲj], written 'ья', because 'я' after the soft sign stands for [j] and [ɑ], as it does after the apostrophe in 'ім’я́'. Its final 'рд' stays voiced, as voiced consonants do at the end of a word.

'Дев’ятсо́т' [dɛʋjɑtˈsɔt] keeps the apostrophe of 'де́в’ять': 'в' stays hard and the [j] of 'я' is said. The hundreds from 'п’ятсо́т' to 'дев’ятсо́т' are stressed on 'сот', and the soft sign of 'п’ять', 'шість' and 'де́в’ять' is not written before it. In 'шістсо́т' [ʃiˈsːɔt] the 'т' between two 'с' is not pronounced, as in 'шістна́дцять', and the two 'с' make one long [sː].

The instrumental forms in '-ма' are stressed on the ending. In 'п’ятьма́' and 'шістьма́' the soft sign makes the 'т' before 'м' soft, as in 'дітьми́', while 'чотирма́' has a hard 'р' and no soft sign.

'Столі́ття' [stɔˈlʲitʲːɑ] and 'десятилі́ття' have a doubled 'тт', a long soft [tʲː], as in 'життя́', and 'насе́лення' [nɑˈsɛlʲɛnʲːɑ] has a long soft [nʲː]. The doubling stays before a vowel, as in the locative 'у столі́тті', but not at the end of a word: the genitive plural 'столі́ть' has one 'т' and a soft sign.

Several numerals and nouns change a sound or move their stress in other forms:

- 'ві́сім', 'восьми́'; 'сім', 'семи́'; 'шість', 'шести́': the 'і' of a closed syllable is 'о' or 'е' in an open one, as in 'кіт', 'кота́', in the forms in '-и' only
- 'со́рок', 'сорока́': the stress moves to the ending
- 'о́бидва', 'обо́х': the stress moves from the first syllable to the last
- 'рік', 'ро́ці': the 'і' of the closed syllable is 'о' in the open one, as in 'ро́ку', and 'к' becomes 'ц' before the locative ending '-і'
- 'відсо́ток', 'відсо́тка': the 'о' before 'к' drops when an ending is added, as in 'ри́нок', 'на ри́нку'
- 'рахува́ти', 'раху́ю': '-ува-' becomes '-у-' in the present, as in 'працюва́ти', 'працю́ю'
- 'стано́вити', 'стано́влю': an 'л' appears after 'в' in the 'я' form, as in 'люби́ти', 'люблю́'

'В' before a consonant is [w], as in 'півтора́' [piwtɔˈrɑ] and 'народи́вся' [nɑrɔˈdɪwsʲɑ]; in 'чверть' [t͡ʃʋɛrtʲ] it stands before a vowel and is [ʋ]. In 'відсо́ток' [ʋidˈsɔtɔk] the 'д' stays voiced before 'с', as voiced consonants do in careful speech.

culture.title: Writing numbers, and the dates of independence
culture.text:
Ukrainian writes numbers a little differently from American English. A space separates the thousands where English uses a comma, and a comma separates the whole number from the decimals where English uses a period:

- 1 500 is fifteen hundred, 'ти́сяча п’ятсо́т'
- 1 000 000 is a million, 'мільйо́н'
- 2,5 is two and a half

News reports shorten the large numbers: 'тис.' stands for 'ти́сяча', 'млн' for 'мільйо́н' and 'млрд' for 'мілья́рд'. A year in writing is often followed by 'р.', short for 'рік' in whatever form the sentence needs, and a reader says the full words: '1991 р.' is read 'ти́сяча дев’ятсо́т дев’яно́сто пе́рший рік'. Centuries are written in Roman numerals, so 'XX столі́ття' is read 'двадця́те столі́ття'. In everyday speech a year of the last century is often shortened to its last two words, as English says 'ninety-one': 'у дев’яно́сто пе́ршому', in ninety-one.

Two dates of 1991 mark the independence of Ukraine. On August 24, 'два́дцять четве́ртого се́рпня', the parliament in Kyiv adopted the Act of Declaration of Independence, and August 24 is Independence Day, 'День Незале́жності', the main state holiday. On December 1 of the same year a national referendum confirmed the decision: more than ninety percent of those who voted, 'бі́льше ніж дев’яно́сто відсо́тків', voted yes.

In 1982 Kyiv celebrated its fifteen hundredth anniversary, counting from the year 482, a founding date that historians chose on the evidence of archaeology. Kyiv Day, 'День Ки́єва', is celebrated every year on the last Sunday of May.

exercises.hint_source: There were two thousand people at the concert.
exercises.explanation: After 'дві' a noun takes the nominative plural, and 'ти́сяча' is a feminine noun, so it is 'дві ти́сячі'. The people counted follow in the genitive plural, 'люде́й'.

choices: The hundreds repeat the rule of the noun after a number: 'ста' is an old plural, as in 'три ро́ки', and 'сот' is the genitive plural, as in 'п’ять ро́ків'.
exercises.explanation: Each hundred is a unit plus a form of 'сто', chosen by the same rule as the noun after a number. 'Дві́сті' has an old form used for exactly two.

exercises.prompt_target: Окса́на ї́де на мо́ре з ___ по́другами.
exercises.hint_source: Oksana is going to the sea with two friends.
exercises.explanation: After 'з', with, the noun is in the instrumental plural, 'по́другами', and the numeral takes the same case: 'двома́'. The form 'дві' exists only in the nominative and the accusative.
'Дзвони́ти' takes the person in the dative, so the noun is the dative plural 'дру́зям' and the numeral is the dative 'чотирьо́м'.

exercises.prompt: In 'Ми жили́ в двох міста́х.', why is it 'двох' and not 'два'?
choices: 'Двох' is used only with animate nouns.
After 'в' meaning 'in', the noun is in the locative, and the numeral takes the locative too.
exercises.explanation: Outside the nominative and the accusative, the numeral and the noun stand in the same case: 'в двох міста́х', like 'в міста́х' without the number.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'I see two students'?
exercises.explanation: Students are people, so in the accusative the numeral and the noun take the genitive forms 'двох студе́нтів'. 'Два студе́нти' would be the form for things, and 'двом студе́нтам' is the dative.

exercises.audio_target: Він народи́вся в ти́сяча дев’ятсо́т вісімдеся́т шо́стому ро́ці.

exercises.prompt_target: Мій брат народи́вся в ти́сяча дев’ятсо́т дев’яно́сто ___ ро́ці.
exercises.explanation: Only the last word of a year is an ordinal, and after 'в' meaning 'in' it takes the locative ending '-ому', with 'ро́ці'. The words before it stay as they are.

exercises.prompt: How do you say 'in the twentieth century'?
exercises.explanation: A century is named by an ordinal, 'двадця́тий', which agrees with the neuter noun 'столі́ття'. After 'у' meaning 'in', both are in the locative: 'у двадця́тому столі́тті'.

exercises.prompt: In 'у ти́сяча дев’ятсо́т сімдеся́тому ро́ці', which numeral changes for the case?
choices: Only 'сімдеся́тому', the last one, an ordinal
exercises.explanation: In a year only the last word is an ordinal, and only it changes with 'рік'. 'Ти́сяча' and 'дев’ятсо́т' stay in the nominative.

exercises.hint_source: My parents met in the eighties.
exercises.explanation: A decade is the plural of the ordinal with 'ро́ки'. 'In the eighties' is the locative plural: 'у вісімдеся́тих ро́ках'.

exercises.prompt_target: Украї́на ста́ла незале́жною два́дцять четве́ртого се́рпня ти́сяча дев’ятсо́т дев’яно́сто ___ ро́ку.
exercises.explanation: In a full date the year follows in the genitive, as 'of' the year: the ordinal 'пе́ршого' with 'ро́ку'. 'Незале́жний' means independent.
Collective numerals are not used with feminine nouns, so two sisters are 'дві сестри́', with the feminine form 'дві' and the nominative plural.

exercises.prompt_target: На вечі́рці було́ ___ студе́нтів із Кана́ди.
exercises.hint_source: There were three students from Canada at the party.
exercises.explanation: The noun is in the genitive plural, 'студе́нтів', so 'three' must be the collective numeral 'тро́є'. With 'три' the noun would be in the nominative plural, 'три студе́нти'.

exercises.hint_source: Both sisters work at the hospital.
exercises.explanation: 'Сестра́' is feminine, so 'both' is 'о́бидві', followed by the nominative plural, as after 'дві'.

exercises.audio_target: Полови́на мої́х дру́зів живе́ у Льво́ві.
choices: A quarter of my friends live in Lviv.
Half of my friends live in Kyiv.
Half of my friends live in Lviv.

exercises.explanation: 'Півтора́', or 'півтори́' with a feminine noun such as 'годи́на', means one and a half, and the noun follows in the genitive singular.

exercises.hint_source: Sam has lived in Kyiv for a year and a half.
exercises.explanation: After 'півтора́' the noun is in the genitive singular. The genitive of 'рік' is 'ро́ку'.
'Відсо́ток' is counted like any masculine noun: after 'два' it takes the nominative plural 'відсо́тки'. After 'п’ять' it would be 'відсо́тків'.

exercises.hint_source: Twenty percent of the students work.
exercises.explanation: After 'два́дцять' the noun is in the genitive plural, 'відсо́тків', and what is measured follows in the genitive too, 'студе́нтів'.

exercises.prompt: Why is 'мільйо́н' written with 'ьйо' but 'чотирьо́х' with 'ьо'?
choices: Both are said the same, and the spelling only records history.
In 'мільйо́н' a [j] is said after the soft 'л', and 'й' writes it; in 'чотирьо́х' the 'р' is soft with no [j] after it, so the soft sign alone is written.
exercises.explanation: 'Ьо' writes a soft consonant followed directly by [ɔ]; 'ьйо' writes a soft consonant, then [j], then [ɔ]: [mʲilʲˈjɔn], [t͡ʃɔtɪˈrʲɔx].
The number of people in a group is said with the genitive 'нас' and a collective numeral, here 'че́тверо'.
After 'з', with, the numeral and the noun are both in the instrumental: 'трьома́ дру́зями'.

answers: Я народи́вся в ти́сяча дев’ятсо́т дев’яно́сто пе́ршому ро́ці.
Я народи́лася в ти́сяча дев’ятсо́т дев’яно́сто пе́ршому ро́ці.
Я народи́вся в ти́сяча дев’ятсо́т дев’яно́сто пе́ршому.
Я народи́лася в ти́сяча дев’ятсо́т дев’яно́сто пе́ршому.
exercises.explanation: A man says 'народи́вся' and a woman 'народи́лася'. Only the last word of the year is an ordinal, in the locative with 'ро́ці', and 'в' follows the vowel of the verb.
'Полови́на' is a singular noun, so the verb is singular, and the students follow in the genitive plural.

exercises.prompt_source: The population of the city is one and a half million.
My grandfather was born in the twentieth century.

exercises.prompt: In the first dialogue, how many people did the survey ask?
exercises.explanation: Taras answers 'Ти́сячу.', the accusative of 'ти́сяча', and Sam thinks a thousand out of three million is too few.

exercises.prompt: In the first dialogue, what percentage of people walk to work?
exercises.explanation: 'П’ятна́дцять відсо́тків хо́дять на робо́ту, бо живу́ть бли́зько.' Forty percent take the metro and a quarter, twenty-five percent, take the bus.

exercises.prompt: In the second dialogue, how many years are there between Oksana and her brother?
exercises.explanation: Her brother was born in 1996 and she was born in 2004: 'Між на́ми ві́сім ро́ків.' Three years is the difference between her grandparents.
